findings.description: Critical: The 20-stub batch limit does not bound the number of batches or the retained backlog, while every non-supervisor fingerprint change deliberately re-scores the entire backlog. A large or steadily growing candidate store can therefore trigger unbounded model dispatches, latency, and cost in one cycle.
findings.resolution: Add a deterministic per-cycle dispatch budget (maximum candidates and/or batches), define pagination or carry-forward ordering for work beyond the budget, and add acceptance scenarios proving a large backlog cannot cause unbounded dispatch.

findings.description: Critical: The plan defines validation of completed score documents but no timeout, retry, partial-batch, or fallback behavior when the rubric sub-agent fails, returns no document, or only some batches complete. That leaves the cycle's external-model failure mode and the safety of prior cache/digest reuse undefined.
findings.resolution: Specify bounded timeout/retry behavior and an all-or-nothing scoring transaction. Define whether a failed batch aborts while preserving the prior valid digest, degrades to valid same-fingerprint caches, or emits a degraded no-update result, and test partial multi-batch failure.

findings.description: Critical: Ranking and digest generation trust the rubric document's model-produced scored_at value as the staleness clock and generated_at value, but the schema validates only date-time syntax. A hallucinated, stale, or future timestamp can alter penalties, ordering, and persisted evidence time without detection.
findings.resolution: Make evidence time a host/script-owned input, or validate scorer timestamps against a host-provided bounded clock before ranking. Add tests for future, stale, naive, and cross-batch timestamps and define one deterministic generated_at rule.

findings.description: Critical: The design assigns bounded provenance loading and deterministic batch construction to digest.py, but its declared CLI exposes only store, rank, digest, stub-to-request, and decide. The host-dispatched scoring workflow therefore lacks a concrete callable contract for producing the sanitized batch payload that the rubric prompt consumes.
findings.resolution: Define a public prepare-batches CLI/API and its schema, including fresh/retained inputs, ready-set input, size accounting, deterministic chunk IDs, degraded evidence, and stdout/file behavior under dry-run; then wire that exact interface into tasks and SKILL.md.

findings.description: Nit: D6 ends with the incomplete sentence 'A due deferral is the explicit', leaving the unchanged-fingerprint exception rationale unfinished.
findings.resolution: Complete the D6 sentence with the intended due-deferral behavior or remove the fragment.

findings.description: Nit: D8 ends mid-sentence after 'Multi-batch scores are exact-set validated,' so the security-boundary decision is visibly incomplete.
findings.resolution: Complete the D8 sentence and state the intended all-batch validation/write ordering.

findings.description: The plan correctly treats provenance as untrusted, bounds contained regular-file reads, rejects symlinks and URIs, redacts secrets, and preserves the host-assisted no-network invariant.
findings.resolution: Retain these explicit boundary checks and negative tests during implementation.

findings.description: The plan correctly installs runtime schemas outside the archivable change directory and routes roadmap mutation through refine-roadmap's preview/base-SHA transaction.
findings.resolution: Retain byte-identical runtime schema tests and the stale-SHA integration scenario.
